A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same training-free style-personalization work using scale-wise autoregressive models, despite retitling and substantial methodological revision. All pages, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original prompt-injection experiments, benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations including appendix Table 2, and a 40-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 reports original SVD intervention experiments, benchmark and ablation results, sensitivity analyses, a 30-participant user study, and qualitative experiments on additional backbones.

M1.justification: v1's three-path system uses feature initialization, Key Stage Attention Sharing at steps 2–3, and similarity-weighted Adaptive Query Sharing at steps 4–7. v2 replaces this with two generation streams conditioned on the same prompt, SVD-based Principal Feature Blending at the third feature, and Structural Attention Correction replacing content queries and keys at steps 3–12. These change the inference procedure, rather than merely renaming components.

E1.justification: The 190-prompt Parti benchmark, ten quantitative reference styles, and image-guided and text-only generation tasks remain. Qualitative artistic-style coverage changes: v2 includes geometric flat illustration, metallic 3D, neon comic art, and retro sci-fi examples, while earlier Mesopotamian-relief examples disappear. Additional backbones change model settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 add CSGO and StyleAR to the six retained external baselines. B-LoRA joins the user-study comparison. For text-only style-aligned generation, v2 Figure 14 adds comparisons against StyleAligned and AlignedGen, whereas v1 Figure 8 displays only the proposed method.

E3.justification: v2 adds the harmonic mean of prompt and style fidelity as an evaluation metric. The user study changes from 40 participants choosing among four methods to 30 choosing among five. New experiments introduce mixed object/color prompt-pair controls and evaluation on Infinity-8B and Switti. The primary Infinity-2B benchmark, output resolution, and stated GPU remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The step-wise prompt-injection analysis is retained, but the query/key/value replacement analysis is replaced by baseline, full-feature replacement, and SVD-guided controls. Component ablations are redesigned around replacement, PFB, and SAC. Appendix A adds top-k singular-component and exponential-decay sensitivity studies, and Appendix D tests qualitative generalization across backbones.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional averaged CLIP results and the revised user-study sample size do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: On the retained benchmark, Table 1 changes the proposed method's prompt fidelity from 0.330 to 0.334, style fidelity from 0.603 to 0.630, and reported runtime from 6.44 to 3.58 seconds; the six shared baselines' corresponding values remain unchanged. v2 adds baseline, harmonic-score, spectral-analysis, sensitivity, and backbone results. User preferences change from 57.5%/30.5% to 35.3%/32.0% for prompt/style fidelity, but the changed participants and candidate set preclude interpreting these as comparable gains or losses.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction changes from attention concatenation and cosine-weighted query mixing to principal/residual feature decomposition, an exponentially weighted SVD operator, and residual-preserving reconstruction in v2 Section 5.2. Appendix A additionally defines top-k decompositions and interventions. These substantively revise the formal definitions; neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the central claim about content-specific query representations and attention sharing with a claim that dominant singular components of the third feature encode style, motivating PFB and SAC. Training-free personalization from a single reference and efficient autoregressive generation remain the overarching goals.

C2.justification: v2 explains style/content separation through leading versus higher-rank singular components and interprets weaker spectral decay as increasing content leakage. It also adds an explicit limitation: heterogeneous reference styles can become blended because the method cannot selectively isolate sub-styles. v1 instead emphasizes query-based content control and ends with general future directions.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, the spectral-decay setting, and extensive baseline implementation information, including repository provenance, default configurations, the unofficial StyleDrop implementation, and a shared A6000/PyTorch environment. Table 1 and Appendix C explicitly explain that tuning-based runtimes include style-specific training plus one generated image. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that retained baseline experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references including CSD-VAR, FLUX, multimodal diffusion editing, CSGO, StyleAR, and AlignedGen, and connects the revised mechanism to prior feature decomposition and attention editing. Most of the three-part related-work discussion remains. Publication updates and duplicate entries for existing works do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introduction passages, mechanism analysis, method description, ablation discussion, and conclusion are rewritten around the SVD formulation. The appendix is reorganized into analysis, algorithm, implementation, backbone experiments, limitations, and qualitative-results sections. This substantially changes the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline schematic and replaces the attention-feature illustration with a spectral-analysis display. It expands the comparison table, changes the ablation-table structure and placement, adds sensitivity plots and a user-preference table, and revises qualitative grids. Typography, author presentation, references, and overall page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence and documentation supporting its revised mechanism. Full-replacement/SVD controls, component ablations, and rank/decay sweeps provide more diagnostic support than v1's narrower attention-sharing analysis. Algorithm and baseline documentation address important reproducibility gaps, while timing clarification and explicit mixed-style limitations improve transparency. The smaller, redesigned user study cannot establish a preference improvement, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these limits do not outweigh the substantial gains in mechanistic support and reproducibility.
